headline: Genetic and transcriptomic annotation narrows candidate genes in complex disease loci
label: Functional Genomics Target Prioritization
summary: Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and multi-omic QTL resources now link GWAS loci to effector genes and their regulatory contexts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of genetic association, quantitative trait, and regulatory annotation to narrow candidate genes and mechanisms. Mendelian randomization with colocalization against eQTL, mQTL, or pQTL data recurs in items on adenomyosis exosome-related genes, heart failure immune drivers (65 genes), sepsis mitochondrial genes, and SLE with bladder cancer. Airway GWAS integration via LDSC, Genomic SEM and MTWAS defines a shared latent architecture across COPD, asthma, bronchiectasis and CRSsNP. The adipocyte multiome across 118 donors is new in resolving context-dependent cis-regulatory and cellular program QTLs under metabolic stimuli. Other items rely on transcriptomic reanalysis, regulatory network reconstruction (nf-sarcopipe, IPF, skeletal muscle T2D), or multi-omic profiling without a genetic-causal step.
